items.claim: Prov.25.19's 'simile' device label rests on the English gloss 'likened to' with zero Hebrew quoted for that specific claim; the verse itself carries no comparative-particle marking.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.25.19 (שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה) has no kaf-prefix or כֵּן apodosis anywhere -- it is direct nominal juxtaposition (bad tooth / slipping foot / treacherous confidence), the same unmarked-equation construction the sibling row at oshb:Prov.25.11-12 (same part) correctly discloses as 'lacking the usual comparative particle-plus-apodosis frame.' The WEB rendering supplies 'is like' where the Hebrew has no comparative morphology (verse_map_web.json Prov.25.19: 'is like a bad tooth'), and this row's only quoted Hebrew run (the ביום phrase) supports an unrelated phrase-extension-trap point, not the simile claim itself. Contrast the book's genuinely marked simile at oshb:Prov.26.18-19 (כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ...כֵּֽן), confirming the absence here is a real construction difference, not an extraction gap.
tier_citations: web (verse_map_web.json Prov.25.19 'is like' -- translation-only, not in the Hebrew)

items.claim: Prov.26.4-26.5's observed_substrate_signals overclaims the repeated closing phrase as 'byte-identical across the pair'; the opening word of that phrase differs by one dagesh between the two verses.
items.evidence: Codepoint comparison of oshb:Prov.26.4 and oshb:Prov.26.5 shows the first word of the phrase, כְּ֭סִיל (26:4) vs כְ֭סִיל (26:5), carries an extra dagesh (U+05BC) after the initial kaf in 26:4 that is absent in 26:5 -- the row's own quoted text for 26:5 already shows the single-kaf form, so this is a tier-mislabel rather than a mis-transcription. The second word, כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ (26:4) / כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ (26:5), IS byte-identical across both verses (collate.py: byte tier both refs). The dagesh variance does not disturb the core cluster argument: the reversed governing imperative (תַּ֣עַן with the preceding אל in oshb:Prov.26.4 vs עֲנֵ֣ה in oshb:Prov.26.5) collates at byte tier at both refs, and this remains the book's own documented deliberate-contradiction pair -- but 'byte-identical' should read as a one-dagesh variant in the opening kaf, per tier discipline.
